cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you imagine next grows out of what you have already lived through.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Picture a piece of your life turning out differently than it sits now, hold that picture a minute, and take the smallest next step toward it before the week ends.
cells.core:
You hold momentum with warmth, and that same steadiness is what lets you sit with something unanswered instead of closing it early. The fire stays lit around you partly because you can imagine what hasn't happened yet without needing it resolved first.

The whole shape of things is available to you. You can see how the pieces fit, which means you are free to imagine a piece turning out another way. Picture that going differently than it sits now, hold it that way for a minute, and take one small step in that direction before the week is out. Nothing has to be settled. You are only finding out what it looks like when you move.
cells.sheetLine: You can picture what hasn't happened and walk toward it.
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a future you cannot write in advance, and that bracing has taken the pen.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Whatever you've been holding back for fear of how it lands — say it plainly, kindly, once. Then let it stand without checking whether it was received.
cells.core:
You tend the fire well enough that you can read how the pieces fit together, and right now that reading has turned into guarding. You have started lining up what might happen, calibrating your words before you speak, running the conversation ahead of time. The warmth that usually moves people forward is on hold while you prepare for every possibility at once.

You can say a hard thing without it becoming a weapon. Whatever you are carrying that somebody needs to hear, say it plainly, once, with care for how it lands. Then leave it alone. Hold your clarity steady instead of refreshing it. Some of what you are bracing for won't happen, and what you said will already have said it.
cells.sheetLine: Bracing for every future keeps the fire from warming anyone.
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed in front of you, watching a pattern that already moved on.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: A role, a plan, a way of showing up has finished. Let it be done, keep only the part still worth carrying, and do the next thing that only works once it's over.
cells.core:
You know how to keep a fire going and you can read how things connect, but that reading is pointed backward now. You keep revisiting what already happened, holding the shape of it, because that is easier than looking at what a next thing would need. The fire is banked. There is still heat, but nothing new is catching.

Something you are still tending has already finished. Say what it is, let it be finished, and keep only the part of it that still serves you. Then do the next thing that only makes sense if the finished thing is over. You don't have to want the new thing yet. You only have to stop warming the old one.
cells.sheetLine: You keep warming something that has already gone out.
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it

cells.tense: The pen is down, but you are already writing the next chapter of the room.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: A change you keep seeing is overdue — make one small unglamorous action toward it this week. No announcement, no permission. Just the first real inch.
cells.core:
You can read how the whole pattern fits, and you keep moving things forward, but you aren't naming that movement as yours. The changes you bring get filed under circumstance, good timing, or someone else's suggestion. You notice what is overdue and then act on it without ever writing your own name on what you saw.

A change you keep seeing should happen. Take one real inch of it this week, a small unglamorous action that only makes sense if you are building it. No announcement. The inch is the point. When it is done, see that you did it, and mark it somewhere you'll find it again.
cells.sheetLine: The change you keep seeing is already yours.
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that vision here is already integrated and the person still needs to initiate more of it; a reader could say this is just ordinary planning and the ask adds another task to a full week. The ask survives being wrong because naming one thing that could still turn out differently and taking one step toward it teaches something either way, regardless of whether the read fits. The sentence that serves me more than them is any phrasing that sounds like a verdict on their whole life instead of a description of one hour at a table.
